findings.claim: A dispatch that reaches a target after its validity window is not recorded as a terminal expired rejection, contrary to the remote-dispatch contract.
findings.evidence: The requirement `execution-remote-dispatch` says: `WHEN a queued request reaches a target after its validity window THEN the target records a terminal rejection and never starts a local run`; however `RemoteTarget::receive` calls `self.queue.accept(dispatch.clone(), &self.enrollment, now)?` and propagates `RemoteError::Expired`, while `DispatchQueue::accept` returns `Err(RemoteError::Expired)` before appending any event when `now > dispatch.expires_at()?`.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle expiry in `RemoteTarget::receive` by durably creating/transitioning the target record to `PeerDispatchState::Expired` and returning a signed expired peer response instead of propagating `RemoteError::Expired` before queue insertion.
